llm.summary: The skill appears to be a legitimate Notion sync tool that only needs your Notion integration token, but the package and metadata are inconsistent (the registry says no env vars required while the SKILL.md and scripts require NOTION_API_KEY) and it contains runnable scripts—review before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, SKILL.md and the scripts align: this is a Notion sync/management tool and the code uses the Notion API. However the registry metadata (Requirements: Required env vars: none, Primary credential: none) contradicts the SKILL.md and code which require NOTION_API_KEY. That mismatch could be an honest manifest omission but is an inconsistency you should verify.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and scripts stay within the claimed scope: they call only api.notion.com, read/writes local markdown files, and maintain a small state file (memory/notion-watch-state.json). The scripts do not attempt to read other system credentials or call unrelated remote endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote install/download step (no external URLs or installers); the package includes Node.js scripts that will run locally. This reduces supply-chain risk, but running bundled scripts still executes code on your machine—no install spec is not a security problem by itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only sensitive value required by the code is NOTION_API_KEY (and optional NOTION_WATCH_* env vars for the watcher). That is proportionate to a Notion integration. The concern is the metadata omission: the registry claims no required env vars while the code demands a token—verify which declaration is authoritative before granting credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and uses normal agent invocation. It writes a local state file under a workspace-relative path (memory/notion-watch-state.json) which is expected for the watcher feature. It does not request elevated or cross-skill privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing or running this skill:
- Confirm the NOTION_API_KEY requirement: the SKILL.md and scripts read NOTION_API_KEY but the registry metadata omits it — treat the SKILL.md/code as authoritative and only provide a token you control.
- Scope the token: create a Notion integration with the minimum permissions needed and explicitly share only the pages/databases the integration must access.
- Inspect the bundled scripts yourself (they're plain JS) before running. They make HTTPS calls to api.notion.com and read/write local files (including memory/notion-watch-state.json); no hidden endpoints were found in the provided code.
- Run the scripts in an isolated environment (e.g., dev container) if you are unsure, and avoid giving the token to untrusted environments.
- If you rely on registry metadata for automation, fix or confirm the manifest discrepancy (required env var missing) before deploying in production.
If you want, I can produce a short checklist of commands to run these scripts safely (create scoped integration, test with a throwaway page, review state file contents).
